clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old female presented with three weeks of right tibial pain exacerbated by standing and walking, with local tenderness and mild swelling but no trauma or systemic signs. Initial X-ray showed a well-defined intramedullary sclerotic lesion with a narrow zone of transition and no fracture. Subsequent radiographs confirmed focal circumferential endosteal and intramedullary thickening and sclerosis without destructive features, periosteal reaction, or soft tissue masses. CT imaging further delineated the lesion, demonstrating medullary canal obliteration without sinus, sequestrum, periosteal reaction, or soft tissue involvement. Clinical exam findings were consistent with localized pain and tenderness without neurological deficits. The patient was managed conservatively with NSAIDs and activity modification. No MRI, bone scan, biopsy, or follow-up symptom evolution data were available from the source. Imaging features and clinical presentation supported the diagnosis of IMOS.
